options.text: Open only in the evening.
Open all day except morning.
Closed every day.
Open only in the morning.

questions.explanation: 'Ne...que' limits to one case, so opening is only in the morning.

questions.topic: An idiom about relying on someone
questions.learningObjective: Explain an idiom about relying on someone
questions.stem: The idiom 'compter sur quelqu'un' means to rely on a person.

options.text: It means counting someone's money.
It means ignoring that person.
It means relying on that person.
It means arguing with them.

questions.explanation: The idiom expresses reliance, not counting or ignoring.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: The mood required after il faut que
questions.learningObjective: Name the mood required after il faut que
questions.stem: The costing sheet notes the mood triggered by 'il faut que'.

answer.exemplar: After 'il faut que' the verb must be in the subjunctive mood, expressing obligation or necessity.

questions.explanation: Il faut que triggers the subjunctive because it expresses necessity rather than fact.

questions.topic: Negation inside a clause of exception
questions.learningObjective: Apply negation inside a clause of exception

stimulus.body: The costing sheet shows 'sauf que je ne comprends pas'. The negation remains complete.

questions.stem: Which negation is correct after sauf?

options.text: Only ne is used, pas disappears.
Pas becomes plus.
Negation is removed entirely.
The full ne...pas negation remains.

questions.explanation: The clause after sauf keeps its ordinary ne...pas negation.

questions.stem: Social security branches pay benefits funded by contributions.

questions.topic: The occupational health visit and who may decline it
questions.learningObjective: State who may decline the occupational health visit
questions.stem: The occupational health visit aims to protect worker health.

options.text: Only the employer may decline it.
No one may ever decline it.
The employee may decline in limited cases.
The doctor alone decides without consent.

questions.explanation: The employee may decline in limited circumstances; the employer cannot impose attendance arbitrarily.

questions.topic: Why a fire notice forbids lifts
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a fire notice forbids lifts
questions.stem: During a fire, the lift must not be used for evacuation.

answer.exemplar: Lifts are forbidden because power may fail and shafts can draw smoke, trapping occupants during a fire.

questions.explanation: Power failure and smoke spread in shafts make lifts dangerous during a fire.

questions.topic: A set phrase that asks favourably
questions.learningObjective: Identify a set phrase that asks favourably

stimulus.body: The costing sheet lists polite request formulas. One phrase asks favourably without demanding.

questions.stem: Which phrase asks favourably?

options.text: Tu dois le faire.
C'est obligatoire.
Fais-le maintenant.
Pourriez-vous m'aider ?

questions.explanation: A polite conditional question asks favourably, unlike commands or duty statements.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish anticipating from reporting
questions.stem: Anticipating and reporting describe different time relations to an event.

Both happen before the event.
